title: A Survey of Multimodal Hallucination Evaluation and Detection

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating vision-language models using balanced or paired Yes/No questions in benchmarks (such as POPE, MME, HallusionBench, and PhD) to detect and mitigate the models' inherent tendency to disproportionately output 'Yes' even when the answer should be 'No'.

Employing adversarial sampling of objects that are highly frequent or commonly co-occur in training data, but are absent from the test image, to measure if models hallucinate based on statistical priors rather than actual visual grounding.

Reviewing text-to-image (T2I) benchmarks (such as HRS-Bench) that assess fairness and evaluate whether distributional biases in training data cause models to generate stereotyped outputs that override specific demographic prompt instructions.
